title: Object, block or file storage?

rows.label: You access it through
values: A raw disk mounted on one machine
A shared folder over NFS or SMB

rows.label: Has a file system
values: No. Keys only look like folders; a mount tool can add one on top
No. You format one onto it (ext4, NTFS) before use

rows.label: Shared between machines
values: Usually one VM at a time

rows.label: Rename a folder
values: Copy and delete every object under the prefix
Instant, via the file system on it

rows.label: Typical latency
values: Under a millisecond to a few

rows.label: Reach for it for
values: Shared content, legacy apps, home folders

tip: A typical app uses all three: block storage under its database, object storage for uploads and backups, and file storage only when several servers truly need the same folder. Software that expects files can still use a bucket through a mount such as Amazon S3 Files or Mountpoint, with limits.
